title: On the Balmer spectrum of the Morel–Voevodsky category
summary: Two invalid printed derivations are directly used for core components of Theorem7.6: coefficient-loss conservativity at infinite height, and p-annihilation used in field-equivalence kernel equality. Explicit counterexamples refute the supporting statements; verified local arguments establish the weaker needed conclusions. A separate infinity finite-generation assertion is false outside its actual finite-height downstream use. No counterexample to Theorem7.6 is claimed.

problems.title: Infinite-height annihilator radical is not finitely generated
problems.assumptions: Flexible characteristic-zero k=C(t1,t2,...), any prime p, m=infinity; U is the compact localized unit in the first anisotropy quotient.
problems.original_claim: sqrt J(U) is finitely generated, without a finite-m restriction.
problems.check: Heart coefficients of the localized MGL unit equal Fp[x]; numerical pairing at the point kills no coefficient. The annihilator in L_(p)=BP[x] is I_infinity=(p,v1,v2,...), radical because quotient Fp[x] is a domain. Every finite generator list lies in (p,v1,...,vN); v_(N+1) survives the quotient.
problems.result: Explicit admitted counterexample; finite presentation fails for the same unit's one-term complex.
problems.counterevidence: Finite height has finitely generated I(p,m). The printed7.4 argument explicitly branches: finite m uses this step, infinity instead requires conservativity. The infinity heart is understood using all finite-length norm varieties, not an undefined infinite-length symbol.
problems.impact: No core dependency on the false infinity instance demonstrated; local scope error.
problems.correction: Restrict finite-generation argument to finite m with flexible hypothesis made explicit; separate zero-MGL-motive whole-ring annihilator case.
problems.repair_verification: Exact counterexample and dependency boundary checked; no uniform theorem over nonflexible fields supplied.

problems.title: False equivalence supplies an unsupported core infinity conservativity bridge

location.claim: Opening of Proposition7.1 proof, then last sentence of Proposition7.4 and Theorem7.6(1),(3)

problems.assumptions: m=infinity, R=Fp[x] to K(p,infinity)=Fp; bounded numerical-motive complexes over flexible characteristic-zero k.
problems.original_claim: The coefficient-change functor is an equivalence at infinity; later its composite with the weight functor is invoked as conservative.
problems.check: For p=2, nonzero coefficient x2:T(2)[4]->T survives numerical pairing on Spec k but maps to zero in the target. Thus the functor is not faithful/equivalence. Bounded weight conservativity ends at Fp[x]; it does not automatically imply conservativity after coefficient loss.
problems.result: The printed only stated bridge to the composite conservativity is false. This feeds7.4 infinity->7.5->7.6(1),(3), a demonstrated invalid core derivation.
problems.counterevidence: The Tate map does not refute conservativity; the weaker assertion is true. Prop7.1 alone is invoked only in the finite branch, so merely the extraneous equivalence word would be local if disconnected from p17.
problems.impact: Major under0.7.1 for the explicit main-theorem proof dependency, not for a counterexample to the theorem.
problems.correction: Use coefficientwise numerical CH/p polynomial extension, finite-object positive-degree kernel nilpotence, surjectivity on Hom, lift a target contracting homotopy h, invert q=dh+hd=1-delta via nilpotence, contract by hq^{-1}. This proves conservativity exactly where required.
problems.repair_verification: Full finite-object contraction argument checked; does not assert faithfulness or equivalence.

problems.title: False bare-projector p-annihilation is used in the core field-equivalence derivation

location.claim: Proposition8.5 proof after first diagram; application to7.6(2)

problems.assumptions: p=2, any finite m>=1, flexible k=Q(t1,t2,...), E=F=k(sqrt2), P=R=Spec E; Q comprises varieties whose function fields strictly dominate E.
problems.original_claim: p kills the identity of the bare complementary Cech projector Xtilde_Q, so prime-to-p l can be removed.
problems.check: Q_j>=E forces E into k(Q_j), hence an E-structure by normality. Strictness makes (Q_j)_E anisotropic, so all E-point degrees even and k-degrees divisible4. Spec E(sqrt(t1)) lies in Q, giving exact degree ideal4Z. Under MGL->HZ, H00 of the complementary Cech motive is Z/4; its unit is not killed by2.
problems.result: Explicit counterexample to the printed operative assertion, with every flexibility/finite-extension/equivalence condition satisfied.
problems.counterevidence: The required factorized maps contain M(P) or M(R). A degree-p cover remaining anisotropic after these fields lies in Q and transfer proves p kills those tensor-factor objects, so the needed intermediate conclusion is true.
problems.impact: The false assertion explicitly removes l to produce two vm-factorizations; these give8.5 kernel equality and thus7.6(2). Major under core-derivation criterion; no theorem counterexample.
problems.correction: Replace bare-projector annihilation by p id=0 on M(P) tensor Xtilde_Q and M(R) tensor Xtilde_Q; finite-cover pullback/pushforward supplies it and permits removal of l.
problems.repair_verification: Exact transfer correction checked; scope restricted to the required tensor-factor objects.

independent_acceptance_review.summary: The infinite-height annihilator and nonfaithful coefficient map, and the order-four degree-ideal test for the bare projector, are valid under the stated hypotheses. P1 remains a local Minor scope defect. P2 and P3 each invalidate an explicit core derivation; their verified conservative and tensor-factor replacements do not make the printed assertions true. Major is supported without a counterexample to Theorem7.6.

problem_checks.assumptions: Flexible characteristic-zero field, m=infinity and compact localized unit in the first anisotropy quotient.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: Its graded coefficient ring isFp[x], so the radical annihilator inBP[x] is(p,v1,v2,...). Every finite set of elements of this ideal lies in(p,v1,...,vN) for someN, whilev_(N+1) remains nonzero in that quotient. Hence it is not finitely generated and the asserted finite presentation fails.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The finite-height argument is distinct, and7.4 treats infinity by conservativity rather than5.2; core damage from this endpoint instance is not established.
problem_checks.repair: Restrict the finite-generation statement to the proven finite-height setting; retain zero-object convention.

problem_checks.assumptions: R=Fp[x] reducing toFp at infinity; p=2 permitsx2.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: Nonzerox2:T(2)[4]->T survives the point's numerical degree pairing and is killed by reduction. Thus equivalence/faithfulness is false. For a finite direct sum of fixed twisted motives, every positive coefficient factor raises degree while compensating Chow codimension is bounded, so the reduction kernel is nilpotent and Hom reduction is onto. A lifted target contractionh hasq=dh+hd=1-delta, withq invertible by a finite geometric series;hq^-1 contracts the source bounded complex.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: Nonfaithfulness alone does not refute conservativity. The printed false equivalence supplies the missing coefficient-loss bridge explicitly used by7.4->7.5->7.6(1),(3).
problem_checks.repair: Verified the needed conservative replacement, not an equivalence.

problem_checks.independent_derivation: Strictly dominatingQ_j haveE in their function fields, extending toE-structures by normality; anisotropy overE forces evenE-point degrees and hencek-degrees divisible4. SpecE(sqrtt1) suppliesdegree4, so the degree ideal is4Z. Integral realization of the complementary Cech projector hasH00=Z/4;2 of the unit survives. However the actual maps containM(P)orM(R); a degree-p finite cover killed by the projector, followed by transfer, provesp-annihilation of these tensor objects.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The false bare assertion is used to cancel prime-to-p l in both core factorizations. Tensor-factor transfer restores that cancellation and kernel equality; no theorem counterexample is implied.
problem_checks.repair: Verified the two needed tensor-factor annihilation statements and prime-to-p invertibility.
